notes:
The whole 2.42 series, now on the Stable channel, with touch buttons in every game and Super Mario Strikers. If this console was on 2.42.0, this is everything since.

If this console was on 2.42.0, this update carries a kernel: the console restarts once for the update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not power off while it says part 2 of 2. If a restart stops at the hekate screen, press a button.

New in 2.43.0: touch buttons in every game. In a game's pause menu, Touch buttons, each button runs a hotkey (save and load state, save slots, fast-forward, screenshot, the pause menu, reset, quit, and the Wii shake and recenter) or presses one of player 1's buttons. They stay hidden when a game starts: the Touch buttons on or off hotkey (the game's Controllers, Set hotkeys, any combo, Capture included) or their Hide button shows and hides them. In DS games a touch on a button does not reach the game.

New on Ports and Apps: Super Mario Strikers (Strikers, a native port), from your own disc in the GameCube library: tick it in Add ports and apps, which downloads the port (about 12 MB). The first Play unpacks a compressed disc once (about 1.5 GB). Full speed in matches, and rooms on your local network.

Fixed: with a keyboard or mouse receiver plugged in, the Joy-Cons could go missing from the controller list, so every game said no controller was connected. A game's page no longer scrolls by itself under a resting mouse pointer. On the web page, a zip holding just one .exe asks whether it is the game or its installer, and the answer sticks.

From the 2.42 series: new Xbox (no BIOS needed), Arcade, DOS, PC-98, Master System and Sega CD tabs, a Recent tab, and console tabs you can hide and reorder. New on Ports and Apps, each from your own game: Twilight Princess, The Wind Waker and Wind Waker HD, Melee, Halo with online play, Jak 1 to 3, Sly Cooper and Sly 2, Super Mario 64, Star Fox 64, Mario Kart 64, Perfect Dark, Diddy Kong Racing, Paper Mario, Banjo-Kazooie, Donkey Kong 64, Pokémon Colosseum and XD, Black Ops Zombies and Black Ops II, LEGO Island and Space Cadet Pinball; plus PokeMMO, YouTube, Stremio, PlayStation Remote Play, itch.io and RPG Maker games, and Uninstall for ports.

Play Online for GameCube, Wii, NES, SNES, Genesis, PS1 and N64 games, and Xbox System Link. DS games can run on melonDS DS for achievements and save states, or PokeDaisy for a Pokémon companion. Wii U motion controls and online play, screen filters, PS2 patches and faster GameCube and Wii games.

Controllers: hotkeys per game, two Joy-Con pairs, Bluetooth pads that keep their port, a Wii pointer speed and tilting the console for the Wii Remote, and setting a stick's dead zone by hand. Look and feel: a new look with 13 backgrounds and 3D library views, an interface size and a TV picture size, Settings as tiles, and console logos and colors on themed tabs. Streaming the screen to OBS or VLC is in Settings, Display and Sound. The web page has tabs for phones, browsing every file, games hidden behind a PIN, and copying games over USB-C, with Syncthing and RomM. Performance: a Handheld profile, a GPU max clock, battery limits and one-press RAM tuning. The SCCM Retro app updates hekate and can turn an exFAT card into FAT32 in place, and games can get Home menu icons.

Not yet tried: Super Mario Strikers with real controllers, sound or online play (played here with a virtual controller and the sound muted), and touch buttons in DS games, with a Pro Controller, or docked. Reports welcome.
